description: Catena org-wide Renovate policy. Extend it from any catenahq repo with: extends: github>catenahq/renovate-config. It layers Catena operational config (PR limits, timezone, labels, lockfile cadence, automerge) on top of the generic security baseline github>catenahq/scanctl:secure-base, which owns the 7-day adoption cooldown, GitHub Actions SHA-pinning (first-party actions included), and CVE fast-track. Public on purpose: it carries no secrets, so every consumer (public repos included) resolves it cleanly and the policy stays transparent. The self-hosted runner lives separately in the private catenahq/renovate repo.

No top-level schedule: timing is controlled solely by the single self-hosted Renovate cron (catenahq/renovate, every 4 hours). A Renovate-internal schedule (e.g. before 5am) silently no-ops every run that lands outside the window -- a delayed scheduled run OR any manual workflow_dispatch -- so the same invocation behaves differently by wall clock. Without one, every run, scheduled or manual, does identical work. The 7-day minimumReleaseAge cooldown from secure-base still throttles churn; lockFileMaintenance keeps its own daily window below.

Every update automerges once all its checks pass: CI on the pull request is the gate, and the release bench, the app tests or the deploy that follow the merge carry the proof that it works. No rule here holds a PR for a human.

platformAutomerge is on: Renovate enables GitHub's native auto-merge on its pull requests, and the branch ruleset of the repository (ci / gate) decides when the merge happens. Renovate counts its own aged-release check as passing (secure-base internalChecksAsSuccess), so a repo without such a ruleset would see a branch merge before its CI has even started: a repo must have the ruleset before it extends this preset.

The first-party uses: refs of catenahq/** in workflow and action files (@<40-hex sha> # <branch>) move together in one pull request per consuming repository. The sibling pins in .github/catenahq.lock (lines of the form catenahq/<repo> <40-hex sha> # <branch>) move through pull requests too: Renovate moves each pin to the new head of its branch, one pull request per source repository. A commit has no release timestamp, so these pins skip the adoption cooldown. marcusquinn/aidevops digest updates are on for the same reason.

A `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment above a `*_VERSION` line is tracked in workflow and action files (customManagers:githubActionsVersions) and in Dockerfiles as an ARG or ENV (customManagers:dockerfileVersions), so a tool pinned in a run: block or a build stage is bumped like any other dependency. In ci/run the same comment with datasource=docker above an `*_IMAGE=<image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` line tracks an image pinned by tag and digest.

lockFileMaintenance is exempt from the cooldown (secure-base). A relock re-resolves every dependency inside its existing declared range, which is how most transitive-only CVE fixes reach the lockfile without a direct-dependency bump, so an unmerged relock withholds exactly those. It automerges safely because it changes no declared range and every check on the PR -- including the scanctl diff gate, which fails on any CVE the PR INTRODUCES -- has to pass first.

lockFileMaintenance runs daily, in the window 00:00-03:59 America/Toronto, which one 4-hourly run lands in each day. For a transitive-only fix the relock is the only path: Renovate's vulnerability PRs refuse a change to package-lock.json alone unless lockfileVersion is 1. A run outside the window does no relock; the Dependency Dashboard checkbox starts one at once.

Renovate writes npm lock files with npm 11 (constraints.npm, read before any version a repo's package.json names). npm 12 refuses the registry tarball of any package with bundleDependencies when it writes a lock file (npm/cli#9800, open), which fails the artifact update of every pull request in a repo whose lock holds one, such as @tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions minor and patch bumps: one group.
Container image and compose bumps: one group.

First-party actions and reusable workflows (catenahq/**) are pinned to a SHA with the branch name as the comment (@<sha> # main) and follow the head of that branch: digest updates are on (this overrides the secure-base rule that disables them), with no release-age wait. One group, so every first-party uses: of a consuming repository moves in one pull request.
The sibling pins in .github/catenahq.lock follow the head of their branch, with no release-age wait. One group per source repository.
Digest updates of the SHA-pinned marcusquinn/aidevops reusable workflow.

customManagers.description: Sibling pins in .github/catenahq.lock, one per line: catenahq/<repo> <40-hex sha> # <branch>.
A `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` comment above a `*_VERSION=` line of ci/run, or a `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=...` comment above an `*_IMAGE=<image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` line.
